summary: The four controls intentionally expose visible relationships: workload phase changes the dominant heat source, power scale changes temperature rise, cooling preset increases the sink term, and floorplan mode moves the SRAM heat source.
title: Control Effects

summary: Chip Heat Lab assumes one fixed 96x96 grid, one stylized AI accelerator floorplan, demo-unit block power densities, and a 2D steady-state equation. The output is meant for relative intuition inside this scenario.
title: Model Scope Assumptions

summary: The cooling preset changes `g_cool`, the simplified sink term. Higher cooling in this demo pulls the temperature rise down while keeping the same floorplan and workload.
title: Cooling Demo Explanation

summary: Clustered SRAM concentrates one memory-heavy source in the lower-left middle of the floorplan. Spread SRAM splits that source into two smaller regions, which changes the heatmap and can lower or move the peak in the inference KV phase.
title: SRAM Layout Demo Explanation

summary: The value-loop benchmark asks whether spreading SRAM changes hotspot and peak behavior for a KV-cache-heavy workload before spending cooling budget. It runs the Rust CLI for clustered SRAM, spread SRAM, training with airflow, and training with aggressive cooling, then aggregates the emitted JSON.
title: Value-Loop Benchmark Explanation

summary: Chip Heat Lab is not signoff, JEDEC evidence, foundry validation, CFD, package co-design, reliability analysis, HotSpot parity, 3D-ICE parity, commercial parity, or an accurate chip thermal simulator.
title: Claim Boundaries

summary: The demo equation is `-k * laplacian(T) + g_cool * (T - T_ambient) = q(x, y)`. The implementation solves for temperature rise above ambient with a small finite-difference iteration.
title: Steady-State Equation Reference
